Treating acceptance-criteria.md as a purpose carrier

label: The only authored purpose carrier for a standard packet is spec.md section 2 PROBLEM & PURPOSE, holding a Problem Statement and a one-sentence Purpose; the core template ships the problem anchor and Level 2 requires it.

The problem anchor is enforced only as structural presence: a v2.3+ SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE stamp fails on a missing required anchor, while v2.2 or unstamped documents keep integrity-only checking and content is never graded.

File requirements rise with level while the purpose carrier stays one section: Level 1 requires spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md and implementation-summary.md; Level 2 adds acceptance-criteria.md; Level 3 keeps that set with decision-record.md as a lazy add-on.
A phase parent is validated against the lean trio spec.md, description.json and graph-metadata.json only, so it has exactly one prose document in which purpose could live.
The phase-parent spec template demands root purpose as REQUIRED parent content and provides Problem Statement and Purpose subsections, noting this spec is the only authored parent document.

The phase-parent purpose requirement is unvalidated: phase parents are exempt from anchor checks and the phase-parent template is stamped v2.2, so a parent can ship an empty Problem & Purpose and still pass strict validation.

Two secondary purpose carriers exist but neither is required: goal.md's Durable Directive asks what the packet is for yet goal.md is absent from required files, and description.json's one-line description is the only purpose-shaped field present at every level.

No template or validator surface uses the term user need; the phrase appears only in packet 006 itself, leaving the one-sentence Purpose and the one-line description.json description as the nearest authored slots.

The continuity record every save writes has no purpose field: its fields are packet_pointer, timestamps, recent_action, next_safe_action, blockers, key_files, completion_pct and question ids, and next_safe_action is an action rather than a reason.

direction: Searching for a dedicated user-need template
reason: No template or validator surface uses the term; the answer must name the nearest existing carrier instead.
